content:
WordPress powers a large share of business websites, including many in Gurugram, and it is a good choice when your own team wants to add pages, publish news or update listings without calling a developer. It also has a reputation for being slow and getting hacked. Both problems usually come from how a site was built and looked after, not from WordPress itself. We build, repair and look after WordPress sites from our office on Sohna Road, and this page explains our approach.

Three situations we are usually called in for

1. You need a new WordPress site

A company that wants its marketing team to publish case notes, a real estate developer adding new projects and construction updates, a coaching institute posting batch schedules and results announcements, a hospital maintaining doctor profiles. In each case the structure of the content matters more than the look, so we plan content types first and design around them.

2. Your current site is slow, broken or hacked

Typical symptoms: the admin panel takes ages to load, a plugin update broke the layout, Google shows a "This site may be hacked" warning, or strange Japanese or pharma pages appear in search results under your domain. We diagnose the cause, clean it up, and fix what allowed it to happen.

3. You are moving to, or away from, WordPress

We migrate sites from custom PHP, Wix or older CMS platforms into WordPress, and occasionally advise moving off WordPress when it no longer fits. Either way, every old URL gets a 301 redirect so search traffic is not lost.

How we build: a theme made for your content, and few plugins

Most slow WordPress sites run a multipurpose theme loaded with demo features, a heavy page builder and dozens of plugins. We work the other way round. We build a lightweight custom theme, or a child theme of a well-maintained base theme, and use the native block editor (Gutenberg) with custom blocks for your repeating sections. For structured content such as property listings, courses or doctor profiles, we create custom post types with fields your team fills in, so layouts stay consistent and nobody has to wrestle with design tools. If your team is already comfortable with Elementor and wants to keep it, we can work with it, but we will explain the speed trade-off first.

Our usual toolkit

  • Gutenberg block editor
  • Custom post types
  • Advanced Custom Fields
  • Rank Math or Yoast SEO
  • LiteSpeed Cache or WP Rocket
  • Wordfence
  • UpdraftPlus backups
  • WooCommerce, when you sell online

Every plugin must justify its place. Before adding one, we check its update history and whether a few lines of theme code would do the same job.

Speed and security baseline for every site

  • Core Web Vitals checked on mobile in PageSpeed Insights, with images served in WebP, lazy loading below the fold and unused scripts removed from pages that do not need them.
  • Page caching matched to your host, for example LiteSpeed Cache on LiteSpeed servers.
  • Login protection: no "admin" username, strong passwords, limited login attempts and two-factor authentication for administrators.
  • Least privilege: content writers get Editor or Author roles, not Administrator.
  • File editing disabled in the dashboard, XML-RPC turned off if nothing needs it, and PHP kept on a supported version.
  • Daily off-site backups with a restore tested before handover.

A typical WordPress project timeline

  1. Content planning (week 1): sitemap, content types, which fields each one needs and who will edit what.
  2. Design (weeks 1 to 2): key templates for mobile and desktop, approved by you.
  3. Theme and block development (weeks 2 to 4) on a staging site you can log into.
  4. Content entry and training (weeks 4 to 5): we load the first set of content and show your team how to add more.
  5. Launch and checks (week 5 or 6): redirects, Search Console, backups and a final speed test on the live server.

A 10 to 20 page site usually takes 4 to 6 weeks. A repair job on a hacked or slow site is normally a matter of days once we have access.

What you give us, and what we hand back

We need your content and images, access to hosting and the domain's DNS, and for existing sites an administrator login plus any premium plugin licence keys. At handover you receive administrator access in your own name, the theme source code, a list of every plugin with its purpose, licences registered to your email, and a short recorded training session your staff can rewatch. You own all of it, and you can move to another developer whenever you like.

Where WordPress sites go wrong

  • Nulled themes and plugins. Pirated copies of paid themes are a common source of malware. We replace them with licensed versions or free alternatives.
  • Updates ignored for months, then run all at once on the live site, which breaks things.
  • No staging copy, so every experiment happens in front of customers.
  • A single administrator account held by a freelancer who is no longer reachable.
  • Cheap shared hosting on an old PHP version, which no amount of caching can fully fix.

When we would advise against WordPress

If your site will have five pages that change once a year, a static site is cheaper to run and has almost nothing to update. If you are building a web application with user dashboards, complex permissions or heavy transactions, a framework such as Laravel is usually a better base. And if nobody on your team will ever log in, most of WordPress's advantage disappears. We would rather tell you this at the start than build the wrong thing.

Cost and quotes

The quote depends on the number of templates and content types, custom functionality, the amount of content we enter, and for repair jobs, the state of the existing site. We give a fixed quote after a free consultation, and for an existing site, after a quick audit.

Common questions about WordPress

Is WordPress secure enough for a business site?

Yes, when it is kept updated, uses licensed and maintained plugins, and has proper login protection and backups. Most hacked WordPress sites we see missed one of those basics.

Can my team really update the site without a developer?

For everyday content, yes. We build editing screens around your content, so adding a new project, doctor or course is a matter of filling in fields. Layout changes and new features still need a developer.

Our site was built on Elementor. Do we have to rebuild it?

Not necessarily. We first try to speed it up and clean it. If the page builder is the main bottleneck, we will show you the test results and let you decide whether a rebuild is worth it.

Can you fix a site another agency built?

Yes. We start with an audit of the theme, plugins, hosting and security, then tell you what needs fixing and what can stay.

How often does a WordPress site need updates?

Plugin and core updates come out regularly, so we recommend checking at least weekly, with updates tested on staging first for any site that takes payments or bookings.
